analysis: Examined the .github/workflows/release-provider.yml changes. They are two small edits. (1) Head lines 112-114 add a workflow-level env DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release, with a comment pinning release bytes to Xcode 27.2 via scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh. (2) Head line 1444 (base 1441) changes the older-macOS validation assertion from build_sdk_version '27.0' to '27.2'. Neither touches secrets, permissions, trust-gate logic, artifact digest verification, or signing and publication identity handling. The new env var is a literal, not attacker-controlled, and it is workflow-level, so it is visible to all jobs. That includes Ubuntu jobs and the credential-consuming signing, stage and publish jobs. Its effect depends on scripts that were not supplied (prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and the provider-release-build action). The assertion bump keeps the validation lane strict: it still checks source_commit, release_published and the bundle sha256 against the identity file. It only fails closed if the build SDK version differs. The validation-identity step (base 1099-1109) takes BUILD_SDK_VERSION from env, and the build-and-release job asserts it equals PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION (head line 453). That value must now be 27.2 for the validation lane to pass. That is a consistency requirement, not a security regression. No threat-model entries (A-010, A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054) are weakened. The unchanged publish flow still downloads the artifact by ID and digest, and the unchanged trust gate still verifies the source against master. Remaining unverified contract: the toolchain script and the provider-release-build action, which were not supplied, must really pin Xcode 27.2 and set PROVIDER_SDK_VERSION to 27.2. If they don't, the validation lane fails closed.
